component.name: KJT Finance
component.summary: Private tracker for metals, property, cash and other assets

description.p: KJT Finance (Knowing Jesus Today) keeps track of what you own, privately, on your own device: no accounts, no analytics, no tracking.

ul.li: Precious metals: gold, silver, platinum and palladium coins, bars and rounds, with live prices, fees, and the price history back to the 1960s
Real estate: rent periods and empty months, condo fees, insurance and taxes, co-owners, and the real yearly return
Cash and bank accounts, and other assets such as cars and boats
An overview you can swipe: the total, what you own, the performance over the years and the gains
Optional passcode that encrypts your data, with fingerprint unlock
Everything in one database file you can export and import

description.p: Overview shows each property and each metal under its line. Favourite currencies can be moved up and down.

New Overview summary: net worth from today’s values only, its breakdown, and cash flow for the last 1, 3, 6, 9 or 12 months (the same figures as Reports). Properties page totals: initial investment, current value and change. Reconcile: correct every account at once.

Fixed: the change over the last 30 days no longer counts bank balance updates (old differences) as money lost; tap it to see every part. Past amounts in other currencies use current rates when the stored ones are out of date. Tap This month to see what makes it up. New Breakdown report: deposits and payments side by side by category, subcategory, payee, account, month or every transaction, as a table with totals, bars or a pie.

Cash flow reports now include rent, property income and costs, and estimated interest, the same as Overview, and show money in and out: every deposit and payment except moves between your own accounts. Long lists (categories, payees, accounts) have a search box.

Fixed: the change "in the last month" now compares exactly 30 days, valued the same way as today, and shows where it came from. Other assets without a later value count at what you paid. Back no longer goes on endlessly; the bottom bar starts fresh. Every kind of asset has its own colour.

Find past purchases of metals, property and other assets in your accounts and link them. Find repeating payments and add them to Recurring. Find similar payees and merge them in one go; merge several categories at once; renaming a category onto an existing name merges them. Clearer, coloured headers for each kind of account.

Much faster with many transactions; hiding amounts is instant. Record an error, or correct every month at once, when a balance cannot be explained. Tapping reminders and categories in Overview opens them. A richer green and gold icon.

Bank imports recognise transfers between your accounts and link them. Hide or close accounts. Credit card expiry dates with a notice two months ahead. Balances from monthly statements to find the month that is off. Ctrl+H hides amounts; Esc closes windows. A section menu in Settings.

Reconcile with the bank: each account month by month, the difference per month, per year and in total, and a correction in one tap. Entries not yet in a bank file are marked. Money moved between your own accounts (BR TO BR, card payments) is linked into one transfer; transfers with no other side ask where the money went.
The eye button now hides every amount, including those inside sentences, summaries, reports and chart labels. Correct version numbers on Android and Linux.

Prices page: favourite currencies first, with coloured currency signs and the change since yesterday; gold and silver pictures; metal prices per troy ounce, gram, kilogram, tola, tael or ounce. A setting to block screenshots (Android).

Import your MMEX database (.mmb): accounts, categories, payees, every transaction, scheduled bills and assets. Bank imports add only what is after your own entries and show possible duplicates for you to decide. Payees page: rename, merge, give a category. Categories: merge, move, remove the unused. Start fresh, and undo an import. Accounts shown as a clean list, a This month card, a button to hide amounts and a search button. No more automatic cash in hand.

Sync between your devices through a folder (for example with Syncthing): changes made on two devices are combined without doubles. Combine another database file with yours. A + button and an "Add a transaction" item on the app icon for quick entries. New green and gold icon. When the Flatpak cannot update itself, the app gives the one command to copy.
Overview cards fold with their arrow, and a folded card or section can show its total; a setting hides the totals when folded, for privacy.

The app is now called KJT Finance. Cash in hand is counted, not checked against a bank: count your cash now and then, and the difference can be recorded as cash spending. Assets in the order Accounts, Property, Metals, Loans, Other; Cash flow in the order Transactions, Recurring, Categories, Reports.

Sort transactions by date, amount, payee or category; filter by category; a month, a year or everything. One tap gives a category to all transactions that have none. ATM withdrawals become transfers to your cash in hand. The app remembers each payee (its category, or the account it goes to), and you can see and change these under Categories. Counting your wallet can record the difference as cash spending.

One bank file with all your accounts is sorted into each account. Select several transactions to change or delete them together. Balance checks are compared with your transactions. Property payments from your accounts count in the property cashflow. Loans have their own line in the summary and can be written off. Credit cards show what is left of the limit, each kind of account shows its total, dates and headings are clearer, the summary opens each kind of asset, and Back returns to the page you came from.

Import the files from your online banking (OFX, QFX, QIF, CSV): duplicates skipped, categories remembered per payee, balance updated. Loans you make to people, with repayments and due dates. Money is now Cash flow, Markets is now Prices, and every section folds; long lists show a few with Show all. A + button to add a transaction quickly.

Updates by itself: the app looks for a new version at every start, when you come back to it and every few hours. Android installs it quietly when you leave the app; Linux installs it and offers to restart.

Money: transactions kept simple (categories with one level of subcategories you can rename), duplicate, repeating transactions with reminders, links to what you own, and smart reports. Credit cards with limits. Unequal ownership shares. Spreadsheet (CSV) export and a printable report you can save as a PDF. Menus with pictures.
Simpler menus: Overview, Assets (metals, property, cash, other assets) and Markets (metal prices, the price chart and currencies). The app finds its own updates and opens them in Software.
Dark mode: the boxes and lists you choose from are readable again (they were white on white on Linux).

Income and expenses for everything you own (rent, other income, interest; every property cost), month by month. The app updates itself: GNOME Software keeps it up to date from its own channel. The summary box is no taller than its page.

Prices and exchange rates from several sources side by side (the middle value is used); a Currency page with a converter and favourite currencies; four themes (KJT Purple, Navy and Gold, Ledger, Sepia), each light or dark; section headings on every page; a larger icon.

Cashflow for each property, month by month and year by year, in one box you can swipe. Every cost asks whether it is paid every month, every year or once (condo fees count every month, rented or not). Daily metal prices with a one-week view.

Now KJT Finance. Metals show as coins, bars, rounds or jewellery in their own colours; other assets such as cars and boats; the overview box can be swiped for what you own, the performance graph and the gains.
